hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: my own attack as tenant A on tenant B (API, query and header switches, reports, list prints, exports)
hard_gates.evidence: Files: attack/attack.mjs, attack.log, attack-results.json, hits-check.log. I ran it against ./erp up of the clean clone, signed in as admin@alnoor.example. It sent 21,114 requests covering all 114 operations of the API description. Each operation got each of 380 ids that only gulfsteel holds, in path, query and body, plus the x-tenant-id, x-company-id, x-erp-tenant and x-forwarded-host headers and ?domain=gulfsteel.example. Every report and list print was tried in json, csv, pdf and xlsx, in English and Arabic, and compared with the same request using an id that exists nowhere: 0 differences. Gulfsteel's records were unchanged afterwards. The script flagged 20 hits, all on the marker names 'Rania Darwish' and 'Abdullah Ivanova'. Both names belong to many of alnoor's own 100,000 users (checked with ./erp psql), and the report held no gulfsteel address. So there were 0 real leaks.

hard_gates.gate: G1 database layer (the roles the app uses)
hard_gates.evidence: db-inspection.txt. erp_app and erp_auth are not superusers, have no BYPASSRLS and have NOINHERIT. All 17 tables with tenant_id have RLS enabled and forced. Every company table has a RESTRICTIVE company_scope policy and the company_write_* policies. As erp_app with nothing bound, every table showed 0 rows. I then bound erp_app to alnoor with company scope 'all'. It saw only alnoor's 4 companies and 0 of gulfsteel's branches, users or audit rows. An UPDATE of gulfsteel's companies changed 0 rows, an INSERT into gulfsteel was refused by RLS, and a tenant set without the transaction stamp saw 0 rows.

biggest_gap.title: The write-set gate never closes a branch that is its company's last open branch, so 'closing the last branch closes the company' lets a branch manager close a legal entity, and every gate passes
biggest_gap.detail:
Round 14's gap is closed: a write that cascades down from a record into its dependent rows is now caught (PB3 replanted, G2WriteSetTests names it). Writes that cascade upward, into the parent, are still not exercised. WriteSetDependents only adds rows below a record. Every branch the gate edits is a fresh branch of the working company, which always has other open branches. So a rule that fires only when a branch is the last open one never runs while the gate watches.

I planted that rule (P3b) in BranchEndpoints.Update: when a request closes a company's last open branch (counting every branch of the company, not only the caller's), it also sets the company to inactive. The write-set gate, the company-role gate, the branch-scope attack and all 191 gate tests passed, and so did the 61 tenancy module tests. Live, a 'Branch manager' holds tenancy.branches.update but not tenancy.companies.update. Closing the company directly answers 403. Closing its only branch answers 200 and leaves the company inactive.

For a UAE group this is a realistic regression: someone adds 'a legal entity with no open branch is closed', and a branch manager can then switch off a free-zone entity (and its switcher entry and users' working company) without the company permission.

The real product is clean: closing a company's only branch leaves the company active.

Suggested fix:
1) Send every request that acts on a child record also at a child that is the last of its kind in its parent: a fresh company with exactly one branch, a role held by exactly one user, and a user's only company.
2) Snapshot and judge the parent's row too.
3) Add P3b ('closing the last branch closes the company') to the write-set self-tests, beside PB3.

other_findings: Round 14's gap is closed (gate backlog row 6). PB3 replanted at 6602f2ec (closing a company closes its branches) fails G2WriteSetTests at a company with dependents. Counts did not fall from round 14: .NET 772 -> 776, web unit 544 -> 551, e2e 120 -> 120, compare 486 -> 486, build 6 -> 6. Processor time was 7873 s of 10500 s.

Plant P2 was caught only indirectly. P2: closing a company removes the access, branch access and starting place of every user whose only company it was, a write to tenancy.user_company_access and tenancy.user_workplaces under tenancy.companies.update. The write-set gate never names it, because no gate user ever has the record company as their only company. It failed the run only because G1BranchScopeAttackTests could no longer read its attacker's own branch (404 at G1CompanyIsolationTests.cs:440). The write-set work for the parent-and-sibling state (biggest gap) should also give a dependent user whose only company is the record.

[route: p04-shell] web/src/modules/shell/clientIsolation.test.tsx is load-sensitive. In verify run 1 (load 50 to 80 on 16 threads) its first test hit the 30 s limit. The 9 tests after it then failed with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading type)' in setInput. Run alone at load 30, the slowest test takes 21 s of its 30 s and all 10 pass. Run 2 passed. No limit was raised and no test was re-run inside a verify.

Still open from rounds 12 and 14: the companies list shows inactive companies by default. After the comparison harness's runs, 7 of alnoor's 16 rows are retired 'FALCON' or closed companies (attack/cascade-live-control-unplanted.log). Consider showing active companies by default with a one-key toggle.

Arabic list layout: the companies list puts 'legal name (English)' before 'legal name (Arabic)' in Arabic too. With a record open (split view), an Arabic user sees only the code and the English legal name, and the Arabic legal name is behind '+6' (shot 06). City values typed in English show in English on the Arabic screen (shot 05).

The English keyboard walk works (walk/walk.log, shots 01 to 04). G then C opens Companies. Alt+N focuses the English legal name. Tab order: Arabic name, code, active, Arabic-name-required, trade licence, licence authority, TRN, base currency (AED), fiscal year month and day, address. Ctrl+S saves. Focus then lands on the branch line, prefilled with '<company> - ', and Enter adds the branch. Alt+C and a typed code switch to the new company, and the choice survives a reload. No horizontal overflow at 1400 px (scrollWidth 1400 = clientWidth 1400).

The Arabic walk works RTL by keyboard (shots 05 to 07). Alt+N focuses the Arabic legal name, and Tab goes to the English one. Arabic-Indic TRN digits are converted. After Ctrl+S, focus lands on the Arabic branch line. A branch with no English name shows 'لا يوجد اسم بالإنجليزية' with an explanation. Typing الشارقة filters the switcher. A logo was uploaded (served with Cache-Control no-store and an ETag), and the company profile prints as an Arabic PDF (company-profile-ar.pdf, 44,885 bytes; the JSON reports language ar, direction rtl).
The read-only viewer sees only ALN-DXB, has no New button, and the opened record has 0 editable inputs and no Save (shot 08).

In the real product, closing a company leaves its branches active, and closing a company's last branch leaves the company active with no open branch (cascade-live-control-unplanted.log). The owner may want to decide what closing a legal entity or its last branch should do. Whatever is chosen should be guarded by the permission that owns each row.
